* Phase 13.1: the 17 shared markets, engine catalog and per-vendor listing
  :PROPERTIES:
  :ID:          ips13-shared-markets
  :CHECKS:      cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo test -p index-subscriber -p index-calculator -p index-price-service -p oracle-protocol -p trade-generator && cargo test -p atlas-engine genesis && cargo xtask check workspace && cargo xtask check dep-rules
  :BOUNDARIES:  crates/modules/oracle/protocol/src/source_tick.rs crates/modules/index/subscriber/src/listing.rs crates/modules/index/calculator/src/lib.rs config/index/** config/genesis*.yaml config/services*.yaml config/dev-markets*.yaml crates/services/index/index-price-service/config*.yaml
  :RESERVED:    the 17 markets, their ids 3–19, product types and calendars (13_ref_shared_contract §2); the protocol slots 0–2 kept and every other market removed; Vendor = pyth|stork|kaiko|redstone; the per-vendor starting pins (§3); Coinbase and Hyperliquid removed from the index path
  :END:
  Goal: Reference — `13_ref_shared_contract.md` §1, §2, §3 and §5 (Types, Listing), and `13_ref_index_calculator.md` §1.
  Make the whole stack run exactly the 17 shared markets that Pyth Pro, Stork, Kaiko and Redstone will price, and define the listing every later phase builds on, so the four vendor phases can then run in parallel without touching shared files, and the calculator phase that follows them has one listing to blend over. The 17 markets are settled; `asset_id` = `market_id`, contiguous because trade-generator assigns market ids as `catalog.len()`; quote USD, target_price_decimals 6.
  Crypto (product_type crypto, calendar crypto_24_7): 3 BTC-USD, 4 ETH-USD, 5 SOL-USD, 6 HYPE-USD, 7 ZEC-USD, 8 XRP-USD, 9 NEAR-USD, 10 LIT-USD (Lighter), 11 PUMP-USD (pump.fun). Metals (metal_spot, metal_otc): 12 GOLD-USD, 13 SILVER-USD. US equities (equity, us_equity): 14 INTC-USD, 15 MU-USD, 16 NVDA-USD, 17 MRVL-USD, 18 SNDK-USD. ETF (etf, us_equity): 19 DRAM-USD (Roundhill Memory ETF).
  Engine catalog: keep the genesis protocol slots (assets 0 RESERVED, 1 NATIVE, 2 USDT; markets 0 RESERVED, 1 NATIVE-USDT, 2 NATIVE-PERP), and remove every other market, including BTC-USDT spot and the 20 perps not listed above, from every config under `config/` that enumerates markets or assets (`services.yaml` trade_generator, `services-lane-free-full.yaml`, `genesis-lane-free-full.yaml`, `genesis-lane-free-full-sidecar.yaml`, `genesis-lane-free-demo*.yaml`, `dev-markets*.yaml`; find the rest with `grep -rl KRW-USD config`). Add the 17 as perps with the `price_decimal`, parameter-source row and `hyperliquid_coin` given in `13_ref_shared_contract.md` §2 (new crypto rows copy ZEC-USD's shape; MRVL, SNDK and DRAM copy NVDA-USD's). Update the atlas-engine genesis tests and the trade-generator reference-price tables and tests to the new set. The legacy `oracle-service` configs are not changed.
  Listing: add `config/index/instruments.yaml` (the 17 rows above, each with `price_kind: spot`) and per-vendor fragments `config/index/vendors/{pyth,stork,kaiko,redstone}.yaml` holding the starting pins from `13_ref_shared_contract.md` §3, and `price_kind: spot` as each row's starting value (a vendor phase corrects it, e.g. to `futures_implied`): Pyth all 17 (native_product = Pyth symbol, native_exponent, plus a transitional `pyth_lazer_id` so the existing Pyth source keeps running until 13.3 replaces it with symbology); Stork all 17; Redstone all 17 pinned by ticker; Kaiko the six live-verified `KK_BRR_*` codes, plus a YAML comment for each of the other 11 saying "to locate", so the Kaiko phase completes them. Fragments may carry an optional `overrides:` string map passed untouched to that vendor, and an optional `cadence:` block (`contracted_ms`, `p50_ms`, `p99_ms`, `measured_at`) that the loader parses and exposes read-only; 13.1 writes `contracted_ms` for each vendor (pyth 200, redstone 500, kaiko 1000, stork 500) from 13_ref_shared_contract §3.1. The loader merges instruments and fragments into one row per (instrument, vendor), and rejects: an unknown feed_id, a duplicate (feed_id, vendor), and one native_product used for two instruments by one vendor. Delete `config/index/listings.yaml`, and replace the service config's `listings.path` with `listings.instruments` and `listings.vendors_dir`.
  Types: `Vendor` becomes exactly pyth, stork, kaiko and redstone. Remove Coinbase and Hyperliquid from every index crate, config and test: the `oracle-cex-coinbase`/`oracle-source-hyperliquid` dependencies of `index-subscriber`, their adapters, their listing rules including plan-12's `demo` flag, reciprocal rows and the demo profile, and their service config sections. The crates themselves stay in the workspace for the legacy `oracle-service`.
  Until the vendor phases land, the Stork/Kaiko/Redstone rows are loaded but have no running adapter (13.2 adds the seam), and only the existing Pyth source runs, fed from the fragment's transitional `pyth_lazer_id`.
  Calculator: `MarketTarget` carries a list of per-vendor specs. The interim offer rule is: offer the newest-ts_vendor tick across an instrument's vendors when it advanced past the last offered one (13.7 replaces this with the blend).
  Smoke: `scripts/index-fixture-smoke.sh` uses BTC (instrument 4611686018427387907, asset 3) and NVDA (4611686018427387920, asset 16) baselines against the live vendors. Delete the Coinbase/Hyperliquid fixture harness `scripts/fixture-ws/**`.
  Priorities: exactly the settled 17 and ids; one listing source of truth; no Coinbase/Hyperliquid on the index path; every existing check green.
  Acceptance:
  - `catalog_17_markets_resolve_to_one_instrument_each` (in `crates/modules/index/subscriber/tests/catalog_17_markets.rs`, replacing the 33-market test) asserts that every config under config/ that enumerates markets lists exactly market ids 0–19, that ids 3–19 are the 17 perps above with base_asset_id == market_id, and that each resolves to exactly one instrument in `config/index/instruments.yaml`
  - `instruments_file_is_the_settled_17` asserts feed_id, asset_id, product_type, calendar, quote USD, target decimals 6 and `price_kind: spot` for all 17 rows, with DRAM-USD as etf
  - `vendor_fragments_hold_the_starting_pins` asserts 17 Pyth rows with native_exponent (GOLD -3, SILVER -5, equities -5, crypto -8) and the transitional pyth_lazer_id from 13_ref_shared_contract §3, 17 Stork rows (`*_24_5` for equities), 17 Redstone rows, and exactly the 6 Kaiko rows KK_BRR_BTCUSD, KK_BRR_ETHUSD, KK_BRR_SOLUSD, KK_BRR_XRPUSD, KK_BRR_NEARUSD, KK_BRR_PUMPFUNUSD, and that every row declares `price_kind`
  - `listing_loader_merges_and_rejects` asserts the merged row count and each rejection (unknown feed_id, duplicate (feed_id, vendor), shared native_product), and that fragment overrides pass through unchanged and a `cadence:` block parses with contracted_ms pyth 200, redstone 500, kaiko 1000, stork 500
  - `vendor_is_exactly_the_four` asserts Vendor serializes to exactly pyth, stork, kaiko and redstone
  - `grep -rniE "coinbase|hyperliquid" crates/modules/index crates/services/index config/index` returns nothing, and `config/index/listings.yaml` and `scripts/fixture-ws/` no longer exist
  - `interim_newest_across_vendors_offered_when_advanced` asserts that with two vendors, the newest ts_vendor across them is offered once when it advances and nothing is offered otherwise
  - `cargo test -p trade-generator` and `cargo test -p atlas-engine genesis` pass with the 17-market catalog
  - `scripts/index-fixture-smoke.sh` references only the BTC (…907) and NVDA (…920) instruments, and `bash -n scripts/index-fixture-smoke.sh` passes
  - all existing tests still pass
